caption:
Google made Gemini 4 Argon, its new flagship AI model, broadly available today.
It ranks first on the independent Vals Index, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5.
Developers pay an introductory $2/$10 per million tokens until November 30. In the Gemini app it needs AI Pro or Ultra.

Will Argon make you switch from ChatGPT or Claude?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: VentureBeat · Photos: 9to5Google, Thurrott, VentureBeat, Alchemist-hp / GFDL

slides.headline: Google just dropped Gemini 4 Argon, and it's *beating Claude* on a top AI leaderboard

slides.heading: Ranked *number one*
paras: Gemini 4 Argon scored 68.90% on the independent Vals Index, the top spot. Claude Sonnet 5.5 scored 67.04% and Claude Opus 5.5 scored 66.97%.
Google unveiled Argon on September 30, but only trusted cyber defenders could use it. Today Google opened it to paying users and developers.

slides.heading: *Half the price* of Claude, for now
paras: Developers pay $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens until November 30. Cached input gets a 95% discount.
On December 1 the price doubles to $4 and $20, the same as Claude Opus 5.5. GPT-6 Astra lists at $10 and $50.

slides.heading: Who can *use it today*
paras: Google AI Pro ($19.99 a month) and Ultra ($99.99 a month) subscribers get it in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search. Antigravity access needs Ultra.
Google says Argon answers more directly, with less hedging and less repetition.

slides.heading: Google's own engineers *already run on it*
paras: Over 100,000 Google employees use Argon every month. In four weeks, agentic code submissions rose 35% and rollbacks fell 30%.

paras.t: It is not first everywhere: on Terminal-Bench 4.0 it scored 57.4% to Claude Opus 5.5's 66.4%.

slides.hook: Argon's launch price ends November 30. Follow so you catch every AI price change before it hits you.
